mechanisms.behavior: Create four balls with switches 18-21 occupied. Output 1 ejects from the right end and the working script pulses downstream jam switch 22 as the ball enters the shooter path.
mechanisms.label: Four-ball trough

mechanisms.behavior: Output 2 drives the impulse plunger. The proven table uses power 62, a 0.6 second full-plunge time, and 0.3 random variation; switch 23 is the shooter-lane sensor.
mechanisms.label: Auto launcher

mechanisms.behavior: Switch 51 holds the ball. Output 6 ejects at table angle 220 with strength 25 and force variation 2 in the working script.
mechanisms.label: Right eject scoop

mechanisms.behavior: Unlike Premium/LE, the Pro grave marker does not move. Output 3 enables the static magnet with working-table strength 70 and centered capture; opto 52 confirms ball presence behind the inline drop targets.
mechanisms.label: Static grave-marker magnet

mechanisms.behavior: Output 4 drives the chair magnet with working-table strength 45 and centered capture. Switch 53 detects the captured ball, switch 35 is the standup, and output 18 shakes/steps up the Sparky head assembly.
mechanisms.label: Electric Chair and Sparky

mechanisms.behavior: The Pro uses one physically captive ball and switch 42. It has no Premium/LE hammer coil; impacts alone close the switch.
mechanisms.label: Passive captive ball

mechanisms.behavior: Switches 60-62 are active while their targets are raised and open when hit. Output 12 resets all three targets together.
mechanisms.label: Three inline grave-marker drop targets

mechanisms.behavior: Output 7 raises the post while energized and drops it when disabled. There is no position switch.
mechanisms.label: Loop up-post diverter

mechanisms.behavior: The Pro head has no motorized jaw or latch. A ball rests at switch 54 and output 5 ejects it at table angle 195 with strength 26 and angle/force variation 2.
mechanisms.label: Static snake-head eject

mechanisms.behavior: Dedicated button/EOS pairs D9-D12 drive outputs 15 and 16 through SAM fast flips.
mechanisms.label: Two lower flippers

mechanisms.behavior: Output 8 drives the optional cabinet shaker; omit the physical device only when recreating a cabinet without that factory option.
mechanisms.label: Optional shaker motor

mechanisms.behavior: Optional redemption hardware uses physical service identities 33 to advance tickets, 34 as the meter, and 35 as switched ground, with dedicated switch D19 (public -5) for the ticket notch. These physical functions use the untransported physical.output.ticket group because LibPinMAME solenoid 33 is the synthetic SAM game-on state.
mechanisms.label: Optional ticket dispenser

physical.notes: The reset coil acts on the complete three-target bank. This point is the centroid of exact target centers 60-62, not a claim that the under-playfield reset coil sits on the playfield surface.
This exact VPX slingshot-wall polygon centroid is the manual-confirmed coil assembly projection, with practical uncertainty of about plus or minus 0.02 normalized x and y.

The exact Head1 rest-state pivot supplies the Electric Chair/Sparky step-up assembly point. It is a moving parent-relative coordinate, not an internal coil center.

The official Pro map proves one snake flasher. The table's two callback glow objects sit at the slings and conflict with that physical geometry, so this manual-confirmed snake-eject assembly anchor is used instead of preserving the render error.
The Pro coil chart and location map prove one physical bulb on this side of the rear panel; it is outside normalized playfield space.

The official Pro chart defines optional output 24 as a coin meter. The known-working VPX uses a knocker sound effect for this callback, which is cabinet feedback emulation and does not add a physical knocker to the machine definition.

The official Pro chart proves one captive-ball flasher. The table spreads three glow objects across that area; the central f30a point is retained as one composite physical anchor rather than inventing three bulbs.
